text: 33-year-old woman. The patient reports feeling extremely fatigued and weak, especially towards the end of the day, to the point of difficulty in self-care. speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Given your recent hiking, camping, and exposure to multiple illnesses, have you noticed any specific insect bites, fever, or muscle pain in the areas where you spent time outdoors?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness and fatigue. I also have Mild diplopia.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.

The combination of progressive weakness and fatigue worsening later in the day, coupled with new-onset mild diplopia (double vision), strongly suggests a neuromuscular junction disorder. Given the absence of fever, weight loss, or recent infectious exposure in your history, an autoimmune etiology is most likely. Have you noticed any difficulty with chewing, swallowing, or lifting your eyelids? REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_receptor_antibodies, MuSK_antibodies. REQUEST IMAGES: Slit_lamp_exam_for_diplopia.
